a2-imperfectocontraste-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Rain in the Park
a2-imperfectocontraste-01.scenario: At the language exchange in Hanoi, Daniela asks what you were doing when it started to rain yesterday. You were walking in the park.
a2-imperfectocontraste-01.prompt: Tell Daniela that you were walking in the park when suddenly it started to rain.
a2-imperfectocontraste-01.target: Paseaba por el parque cuando, de repente, empezó a llover.
a2-imperfectocontraste-01.english: I was strolling through the park when, suddenly, it started to rain.
a2-imperfectocontraste-01.canDo: I can understand the core difference: imperfecto = background/habit, indefinido = specific completed event.

a2-imperfectocontraste-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Things at Once
a2-imperfectocontraste-02.scenario: At the language exchange, Daniela asks what you did at home last night. You cooked and listened to music at the same time.
a2-imperfectocontraste-02.prompt: Tell Daniela that you listened to music while you were cooking.
cues: Say what you were doing first
Say what else you were doing at the same time
a2-imperfectocontraste-02.english: While I was cooking, I was listening to music.
a2-imperfectocontraste-02.canDo: I can use 'mientras + imperfecto' to describe two simultaneous past actions.

a2-imperfectocontraste-03.title: Communicative Challenge: How I Felt
a2-imperfectocontraste-03.scenario: Carlos asks you how you felt yesterday when you went into your Spanish class for the exam. You were very nervous and afraid.
a2-imperfectocontraste-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that you were very nervous and afraid when you went into the class.
cues: Say what you did at that moment
a2-imperfectocontraste-03.target: Estaba muy nervioso y tenía miedo cuando entré en la clase.
a2-imperfectocontraste-03.english: I was very nervous and I was afraid when I went into the class.
a2-imperfectocontraste-03.canDo: I can use the imperfecto for past emotional and physical states.

a2-imperfectocontraste-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Wallet in the Park
a2-imperfectocontraste-04.scenario: Daniela asks what happened on Sunday. It was a quiet Sunday, you were walking in the park and you saw a wallet.
a2-imperfectocontraste-04.prompt: Tell Daniela about your quiet Sunday and the wallet you saw in the park.
cues: Say what kind of day it was
Say what you were doing and what you saw
a2-imperfectocontraste-04.target: Era un domingo tranquilo. Caminaba por el parque cuando vi una cartera.
a2-imperfectocontraste-04.english: It was a quiet Sunday. I was walking through the park when I saw a wallet.
a2-imperfectocontraste-04.canDo: I can use both tenses together in an extended past narrative.

a2-imperfectocontraste-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Stormy Night
a2-imperfectocontraste-05.scenario: Meg asks why you got home so late last night. It was midnight and it was raining a lot when you arrived.
a2-imperfectocontraste-05.prompt: Tell Meg that it was midnight and raining a lot when you got home.
cues: Say what the weather was like
a2-imperfectocontraste-05.target: Era medianoche y llovía mucho cuando llegué a casa.
a2-imperfectocontraste-05.english: It was midnight and it was raining a lot when I got home.
a2-imperfectocontraste-05.canDo: I can use the imperfecto for weather, time, and scene-setting.

a2-imperfectocontraste-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: News at Work
a2-imperfectocontraste-consolidation.scenario: At the language exchange, Daniela asks what happened at your office yesterday. You were working when you got an email, and your hands were shaking while you read it.
a2-imperfectocontraste-consolidation.prompt: Tell Daniela what you were doing when the email arrived and how you felt while you read it.
cues: Say what you were doing when the email arrived
Say how you felt while you read it
a2-imperfectocontraste-consolidation.target: Trabajaba en la oficina cuando recibí un email. Mientras lo leía, me temblaban las manos.
a2-imperfectocontraste-consolidation.english: I was working in the office when I received an email. While I was reading it, my hands were shaking.
a2-imperfectocontraste-consolidation.canDo: I can fluently distinguish imperfecto (background/habit/state) from indefinido (event/action).
